questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be three vectors such that $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \sqrt{3}, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = 5, \overset{\to}{b} ∙ \overset{\to}{c} = 10$ and the angle between $\overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{3} .$ If $\overset{\to}{a}$ is perpendicular to the vector $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c},$ then $\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right)\right|$ is equal to ____________.

questions.q: Let $P\left(- 2, - 1, 1\right)$ and $Q\left(\dfrac{56}{17}, \dfrac{43}{17}, \dfrac{111}{17}\right)$ be the vertices of the rhombus $PRQS$. If the direction ratios of the diagonal $RS$ are $\alpha, - 1, \beta$, where both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are integers of minimum absolute values, then ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$P\left(- 2, - 1, 1\right)$ and $Q\left(\dfrac{56}{17}, \dfrac{43}{17}, \dfrac{111}{17}\right)$ be the vertices of the rhombus $PRQS$. If the direction ratios of the diagonal $RS$ are $\alpha, - 1, \beta$, where both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are integers of minimum absolute values, then ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2}$ is equal to

Now $RS = \left(\alpha, - 1, \beta\right)$

So, direction ratio of $PQ ≡ \left(\dfrac{56}{17} + 2, \dfrac{43}{17} + 1, \dfrac{111}{17} - 1\right)$

$≡ \left(\dfrac{90}{17}, \dfrac{60}{17}, \dfrac{94}{17}\right)$

Now we know that diagonal of rhombus are perpendicular,

So, $\dfrac{90}{17}\alpha + \dfrac{60}{17}\left(- 1\right) + \dfrac{94}{17}\beta = 0$

$⇒ 90\alpha + 94\beta = 60$

$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{60 - 90\alpha}{94}$

$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{30\left(2 - 3\alpha\right)}{94}$

$⇒ \beta = - 30\dfrac{\left(3\alpha - 2\right)}{94}$

$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{- 15}{47}\left(3\alpha - 2\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{\beta}{- 15} = \dfrac{3\alpha - 2}{47}$

$⇒ \beta = - 15, \alpha = - 15$ $\left\{\text{as}\alpha\text{\text{ and }}\beta\text{are integer}\right\}$

So, ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} = 225 + 225$$= 450$
